name: Cedar Creek Commons
headline: A 36-home, all income-restricted new-construction family rental building on Ogden Road in Montrose, with nine homes set aside for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, developed by RealAmerica; it won 2026 Round One federal 9% credits.
why_it_matters: It is a small rural 9% deal that targets 30% AMI and I/DD households by building on a developer's adjacent sites, with city fee waivers and a housing authority tax exemption standing in for cash subsidy.

status.label: Credits awarded; closing and construction start not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA lists the award as of 2026-09-30. The application said construction could start in 2026 after an award, but no public record found shows a closing, permit or groundbreaking.

next_step: Watch for the City of Montrose administrative site plan approval and building permit, and for the parcel's conveyance from Black Canyon Flats, LLC to the project.

key_numbers.meaning: 9 at 30% AMI, 9 at 50% AMI and 18 at 60% AMI; 12 one-bedroom, 18 two-bedroom and 6 three-bedroom.
About $15.9 million over the 10-year credit period (inferred); CHFA lists no state credit for this deal.
Community Integration units, with leasing help and services from Community Options Inc.

key_numbers.value: Fee waivers and a tax exemption
key_numbers.meaning: The application says the city expects to waive permit, plan check and use-tax costs, and the Montrose County Housing Authority will provide a property and sales tax exemption.

facts.value: 65890 Ogden Road, Montrose (CHFA award report); the application lists TBD Ogden Road, Montrose 81401
One three-story, wood-frame walk-up building with three stair cores, slab-on-grade foundation
All ground-floor units (25%) designed as Type A accessible units
NGBS Silver planned; all-electric-ready and solar-ready design; six EV-ready parking spaces
Excess acreage next to RealAmerica's Residences at Dry Cedar Creek and Black Canyon Flats, immediately east of the Montrose Recreation Center
Special Populations (I/DD set-aside) and non-metro county of 180,000 or fewer people

money.note: Annual credit for 10 years; CHFA's award descriptions list no state credit.
Application names RBC as the syndicator for federal and state equity.
Application assumes NBH Bank for construction and permanent financing.
Application also requested a 1.25% developer fee boost for serving Special Populations at or below 30% AMI.
Anticipated administrative waiver of building permit fees, plan check fees and city construction use tax upon award; help with sidewalk; city may explore lodging tax funds.
Property and sales tax exemption, per the application.

parties.role: General contractor and property manager (developer's own affiliates, per application)
parties.name: RealAmerica Construction; RealAmerica Management

background.text: Land: the parcel is owned by Black Canyon Flats, LLC, an affiliate formed for RealAmerica's earlier middle-income development next door, and is to be conveyed to RealAmerica Development, LLC under an executed purchase and sale agreement.

Neighbours: Residences at Dry Cedar Creek, RealAmerica's 48-unit 9% property on Ogden Road beside the recreation center (42 units at or below 60% AMI and six market-rate), broke ground in October 2023 and, per the application, opened in October 2024 with a 221-household waitlist.
Black Canyon Flats, the adjacent RealAmerica development serving 80% to 100% AMI households, is described in the application as Proposition 123-supported and expected to open in fall 2026.
Approvals: zoning is already in place, and site plan approval and building permits go through the city's administrative review; no approval record for this project was found online.
The application followed a CHFA concept meeting on 2026-01-13, after which the mix was revised to add one more 30% AMI unit; it was RealAmerica's first 9% application for this project.
Market study cited in the application: 25.6% overall capture rate, 28.1% capture rate for the I/DD units, six LIHTC properties (247 units) in the market area, all full with waitlists.
Supportive services: the operating budget includes $20,000 a year for service coordination and resident activities, tied in the application to the developer fee boost.
Letters of support listed: City of Montrose, Montrose Economic Development Corporation, Montrose Recreation Center, Montrose County Housing Authority and Community Options.

Residences at Dry Cedar Creek opens (per application)

Listed on CHFA's 2026 Round One award report with $1,589,628 federal 9% credit

discrepancies.text: The CHFA award report gives the address as 65890 Ogden Road, the Letters of Intent report gives 65880 Ogden Road, and the application gives TBD Ogden Road.

The credit figures differ by stage: the Letters of Intent report shows $1,800,000 federal and $500,000 state requested, the application narrative says $1,354,379 federal and $500,000 state, and the award is $1,589,628 federal with no state credit.
The Letters of Intent report codes the deal as Special Populations as well as individual/family, but the award report codes it only as new construction, individual/family.
The application calls the neighbouring 9% property both Residences at Cedar Creek Commons and Residences at Dry Cedar Creek; Montrose Press calls it Residences at Dry Cedar Creek.

open_questions: Why the award has no state credit and a federal amount above the narrative's request is not explained publicly.
Total development cost, equity price, loan amount, land price and rents are not public.
No city site plan, permit or closing record for this project was found; no public site plan or rendering was found.
The Proposition 123 award behind Black Canyon Flats is stated only in the application and was not checked against an OEDIT/CHFA award list.
Affordability period and any project-based vouchers are not stated in public sources found.
